---
title: "Yield Criteria: Von Mises vs Tresca"
---

## Equivalent stress measures

$$
\sigma_{VM} = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}\left[(\sigma_1-\sigma_2)^2+(\sigma_2-\sigma_3)^2+(\sigma_3-\sigma_1)^2\right]}
$$

$$
\sigma_{Tresca} = \sigma_{max}-\sigma_{min}
$$

Both are pressure-independent — motion purely along the hydrostatic axis
($\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\sigma_3$) never triggers yield under either criterion. Projected onto
the π-plane, Von Mises is a circle and Tresca is a hexagon inscribed inside it, touching
exactly at the uniaxial-stress corners.

```{=html}
<iframe class="interactive-frame" src="../interactives/pi_plane_yield.html"></iframe>
```

The two criteria always agree at the hexagon's corners and diverge most at the
edge midpoints (pure-shear states), where Tresca is more conservative by $2/\sqrt{3}\approx1.155$.
